Outcome_variable.evidence_source: [/page/5/Text/13] To test the longitudinal relations between sense of identity and LS, an LGM was conducted. Three LGMs (i.e., synthesis, confusion, and LS) were included in one model, but this model did not converge. Hence, two patterns of LGMs, that is, synthesis and LS, and confusion and LS, were conducted. For synthesis and LS, this model did not converge. Thus, the relationship between synthesis and LS was examined by two steps. First, factor scores of the intercept and slope for synthesis were outputted. Second, the factor scores of the intercept and slope were included as observed variables in an LGM for LS, and their relationships with the intercept and slope of LS were examined, S-B\chi^2(12) = 42.286, p < .001, CFI = .994, RMSEA = .045, 90% CI [.031, .060]. Meanwhile, the model consisting of confusion and LS did converge, S-B\chi^2(28) = 134.563, p < .001, CFI = .980, RMSEA = .055, 90% CI [.046, .064].
